input.prompt: Generate a symmetric tilt grain boundary (STGB) in an aluminum system using LAMMPS. The simulation should use metal units, and define a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice structure with a lattice constant of 4.05 Å. Define a three-dimensional simulation box with periodic boundary conditions in all directions. Employ the Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potential for Aluminum. Create two atomic regions: an upper region with lattice orientation (x: [0 3 1], y: [0 -1 3], z: [1 0 0]) and a lower region with lattice orientation (x: [0 3 -1], y: [0 1 3], z: [1 0 0]). Populate these regions with atoms according to their respective orientations to form a Σ5(310) symmetric tilt grain boundary. To remove unrealistic atomic overlaps, displace one region if necessary and delete overlapping atoms when the nearest neighbour distance is below a threshold of 0.35 Å. Compute relevant atomic properties, including centrosymmetry and per-atom potential energy, to assess the structural quality of the generated grain boundary. Perform an initial energy minimization using the conjugate gradient (CG) algorithm with energy and force tolerances of 1e-15 and a maximum of 5000 iterations. Save the minimized configuration in a dump file. Conduct a second energy minimization while allowing the simulation box to relax in the direction perpendicular to the grain boundary to ensure an energetically stable configuration. Save the final minimized structure using the write_data command in LAMMPS data format. Calculate the grain boundary energy using a reference bulk energy per atom of −3.360000 eV. Compute the total system energy, subtract the bulk energy contribution, and normalize by the grain boundary area. Convert the result to mJ/m² and round the final value. As the final output, return the computed grain boundary energy in mJ/m².

Initialize a 3D aluminum bicrystal in LAMMPS. Use metal units and define a simulation box with periodic boundary conditions in all directions. Create a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice with a lattice constant of 4.05 Å. Define two atomic regions to form a symmetric tilt grain boundary (STGB): an upper region with lattice orientation (x: [0 3 1], y: [0 -1 3], z: [1 0 0]) and a lower region with lattice orientation (x: [0 3 -1], y: [0 1 3], z: [1 0 0]). Populate each region with atoms according to their respective orientations. Save this structure using the write_data command in LAMMPS in initial_structure.xyz. As the final output, return the absolute path of the structure file. The input script used for this simulation should be named subtask_1.in.

You are given the absolute path of the initialized aluminum bicrystal structure. Read that structure file and perform energy minimization using the conjugate gradient (CG) method. Set the energy and force tolerances to 1e-15 and run the minimization for up to 5000 iterations. Output thermodynamic data every 10 steps, including total potential energy, box dimensions, and pressure components. Save the minimised structure using the write_data command in LAMMPS in minimised_structure.xyz. As the final output, return the absolute path of this minimised structure file. The input script used for this simulation should be named subtask_2.in

You are given the absolute path of the relaxed atomic structure after the first energy minimization. Read this structure file and perform a second energy minimization while allowing the simulation box to relax perpendicular to the grain boundary. Use the conjugate gradient (CG) minimization method with a tolerance of 1 × 10^-15 for both energy and force, and a maximum of 5000 iterations. As the final output, return the minimised energy in eV units. The input script used for this simulation should be named subtask_3.in

You are given the total minimised energy of a grain boundary in eV and its structure file. Compute the grain boundary (GB) energy by subtracting the reference bulk energy (−3.360000 eV)  from the total minimized energy, normalizing it by the grain boundary area. The grain boundary area is defined as twice the product of the simulation box dimensions in the x and z directions. Report the final GB energy in mJ/m². Print the computed grain boundary energy and return it as the final output. The input script used for this simulation should be named subtask_4.in
